correctness.rationale: For named parameters in the homogeneous strict poset, every complete nonalgebraic singleton type is determined by its lower ideal L and upper filter U. Disjointness and strict comparability L<U are necessary and, with ideal/filter closure, sufficient for transitivity of the one-point extension. The coefficient of v comes only from singleton filters, exactly the maximal elements (leaves). For a leaf at depth k, its strict ancestors form a k-element chain and the eligible L are precisely its k+1 initial segments, including the empty ideal. This gives one contribution at each d from 0 through k and proves the full extraction formula, the adjacent-difference formula and the leaf-depth sum, including the root-only tree. Setting v=0 leaves the exact ideal-size enumerator; conditioning on inclusion of the root gives I_T=1+u times the product of the child polynomials (i.e. 1+u∏ I_child). Exact grouping of complete nonplane child-multiset enumerations gave 1,1,2,4,9,20,48 shapes and one size-seven doubleton, with no earlier collision. The witness coefficient lists match; their v-linear rows are 3+3u+2u²+u³+u⁴ and 3+3u+3u²+2u³. The ideal polynomial has degree equal to the number of vertices, so different sizes cannot collide.
residual_risks: Minimal collision claims are only through size seven; the all-size leaf-depth identity is symbolic and does not assert complete reconstruction by the bivariate invariant.

evidence: Every nonempty rooted-tree ideal is a connected vertex set containing the root, and conversely. Thus the local/root-containing subtree polynomial is exactly I_T−1 with the same size grading. The global all-subtree polynomial counts subtrees not necessarily through the root.
An antichain-size enumerator is different: on a three-vertex chain it is 1+3u rather than 1+u+u²+u³. The usual ideal enumerators satisfy I_(P dual)(u)=u^|P| I_P(1/u).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: An exact minimal collision theorem for the local subtree-size polynomial would cover the marginal collision. A theorem about the global polynomial, antichain cardinality, or all order duals does not directly do so; branching rooted-tree duals generally have several minimal elements. No such local collision statement was verified.
